Subject: Technical deep dive — proposed rotating cadence & next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed way forward so we can lock the deep dive into calendars: 

Recap (TL;DR)
- Goal: 60-minute technical deep dive focused on inference latency profile for batch vs streaming, private deployment options, and KV cache sizing for your EHR ingestion workload.
- Attendees we think are useful: your infra lead + data privacy lead; our solutions engineer (Monica) + product lead (Ben) + myself.
- Key ask from AstraMed: deterministic 95th percentile latency under 2s for clinical search queries; compatibility with your on-prem KMS.

Scheduling ask
- Because the team is spread across US / EU / APAC, we recommend a rotating weekly slot (keeps meeting burden even across regions). Proposed pilot: 6-week rotating cadence (each week a different region’s friendly window).
- Please review the three high-level slots below and tell us which you prefer or suggest alternatives:
  1) US-morning friendly (Mon 15:00–16:00 UTC / 08:00–09:00 PDT) — focused for your West Coast engineers
  2) EU-afternoon friendly (Tue 14:00–15:00 UTC / 15:00–16:00 CEST) — easier for EU product & infra
  3) APAC-evening friendly (Wed 03:00–04:00 UTC / 12:00–13:00 JST) — late for APAC but workable for on-call and Singapore office

Attachments: I’ve included a short agenda and a starter mutual action plan so we can assign owners before the first session.
- redwood-deepdive-agenda.pdf (attached)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (attached)

If you’re good with the rotating approach, we’ll create a recurring series and share a short pilot playbook. If you prefer a static weekly slot, tell us which of the three above works best and we’ll lock it.

Next step: can you share 1–2 preferred options from the three above by EOD Monday? We’ll follow up with a calendar invite and prep notes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Rishi —

Appreciate the summary. We’re keen to proceed with a rotating cadence; it helps our teams share the load. High-level availability from our side:
- US engineering (Sanjay): Tue/Thu mornings EST (13:00–17:00 UTC works well)
- EU product/infra (Priya): Tue/Wed afternoons CEST (13:00–17:00 UTC)
- APAC on-call: limited but can make a late-night/early-morning slot once per month

Priya and I will be on the thread for scheduling. We’d like Marco (infra) on the first session — he’ll raise networking/KMS questions. I’m attaching a short doc with our initial network constraints so you can eyeball any blockers.

We prefer option 2 (EU-afternoon friendly) as the baseline for the first two weeks, then rotate. If you can circulate a proposed 6-week rotation (with local time conversions) we can thumbs-up and add to our calendars.

Thanks,

On Sun, Aug 31, 2025 at 09:07 AM Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@astramed.com> wrote:
> We prefer option 2 (EU-afternoon friendly) as the baseline for the first two weeks, then rotate.

Thanks — happy to build a concrete 6-week pilot schedule. Below is a simple rotation we propose (each meeting 60 minutes):

Pilot rotation (weeks 1–6) — weekly recurring 60-min deep dive
- Week A (baseline) — Tue 14:00 UTC (EU-afternoon friendly) => 15:00 CEST / 10:00 EDT
- Week B — Tue 08:00 UTC (US-morning friendly) => 04:00 PDT / 09:00 BST
- Week C — Tue 22:00 UTC (APAC-evening friendly) => 07:00 JST (next day) / 03:00 EDT
- Repeat pattern for six weeks (A, B, C, A, B, C) — gives each region two sessions in the pilot

Notes:
- We converted to UTC so your team can map to local times easily. If you prefer a different weekday, we can shift to Wed/Tue as needed.
- We’ll seed the first session with a short technical checklist: model sizes, sample payload, JMX/KV cache targets. The pilot playbook (attached) outlines run-of-show and success criteria.

Can you confirm:
1) Confirm the baseline day (Tue 14:00 UTC) for week A
2) Confirm Marco and Priya are invited to the first session
3) Any absolute blackout dates for September?

If you’re good, I’ll create the recurring invite and include the short playbook + pre-read.

Best,
